title: The Man Who Survived Both Atomic Bombs
notes: No free photograph of Tsutomu Yamaguchi exists on Wikimedia Commons. Portraits of him from 2009 are press images and are not freely licensed. This video therefore never shows his face, real or drawn: his cast entry is face hidden.
Commons holds graphic photographs of casualties at both cities. None are used here, and none should be added. The restraint is the editorial position, not squeamishness.
Every archival URL below was resolved from the Commons API and is a direct file URL.
The bombs are shown through the real cloud photographs (p06, p12) and as light, shadow and diagram. No illustrated casualties, injuries or ruins with people in them.
Guide objects: the red hanko seal (opens and closes the film) and the little train on the route map.

yamaguchi.desc: Tsutomu Yamaguchi, a slim 29-year-old Japanese engineer in a dark 1940s suit and hat, carrying a small travel bag; his face is never shown: always from behind, in silhouette, or turned away under the hat brim

hisako.desc: Hisako Yamaguchi, a young Japanese woman in a plain 1940s kimono-style dress, simple vague face

colleagues.desc: two young Japanese engineers in 1940s suits, Akira Iwanaga and Kuniyoshi Sato, simple vague faces, drawn as a pair

supervisor.desc: his supervisor Sato, a middle-aged Japanese office manager in a 1940s suit and round glasses, simple vague face

crowd.desc: a lineup of 1940s Japanese townspeople and passengers, simple vague faces, mostly seen from behind

cast: tiny figure appears on the map, back to camera
beats.note: Opens on the seal. The audience has no idea yet why.

graphics: not nearby, not the next town

cast: turns back on the edge of the desk
walks toward the waiting tram with his bag

graphics: the tram pulls away without him

cast: arrives in the middle of the field
graphics: a field, edge of the city

cast: looks up, hand shading his eyes

beats.note: Hard cut in. Hold through the full 2.5s silence. Nothing on screen but white.

beats.title_overlay: The Man Who Survived Both Atomic Bombs
beats.note: Title card on the white's own tone. Everything still through the 2s silence.

cast: walk beside him along the platform

graphics: hanko diagram: cylinder · wood or ivory · carved name
beats.note: The explainer beat. Build the diagram around the photo.

cast: hurries back into the office for the seal
graphics: → the reason anyone knows his name
a red dot on the third ring
the light: like a magnesium flare

cast: sits up slowly in the darkened field
beats.note: The field set darkens to brown haze; no injuries drawn.

cast: two shapes emerge from the haze

beats.note: Rhymes with the tram he never boarded. The photo is 500 px wide: native size only, no motion on it.

graphics: ATOMIC BOMB typed, then struck through
a term that did not exist yet

cast: stream out of the city along the roads

beats.note: Deliberately empty. The line is one sentence and the image must not illustrate it. Nothing added.

graphics: red route Hiroshima → Nagasaki animates slowly across s26 and s27
the little train rides the route
beats.note: The strongest single visual in the video.

cast: by the window, arm wrapped in cloth
puts on his jacket and walks out

graphics: no bomb in history had ever done this

beats.note: Same white frame as s08, intentionally. Hold the full 3s of silence. This is the centre of the video.

cast: thrown to the floor in silhouette

graphics: at home when it went off

cast: away from the houses with the baby

graphics: chain: 1st bomb → his burns → ointment → out of the house → alive
beats.note: Hold through the turn and do not cut on the line itself.

graphics: deaf in one ear, for life

cast: an old man at the window, back to us
a school group looks at the record
graphics: so it could tell younger people

beats.note: Quote card on the study's tone. Paraphrase, not a verbatim quotation: no quotation marks on screen. Attribution: Tsutomu Yamaguchi.

graphics: 1 glows red: named in the record
not worth much: both struck through

cast: the turn back for the seal, replayed small on the map
graphics: a field ← he forgot a stamp

cast: the same small figure, older, back to us
graphics: worked · taught · raised daughters · buried a son
